drafted_from: tool:insert-frame-holds-into-a-filmcraft-project-copy row, do-work/filmcraft_insert_frame_holds.py and test/test_filmcraft_insert.py (test_the_command_writes_a_new_project_and_prints_one_answer); the answer was observed by running the command on the test's made-up project and ffmpeg-made correction files
start_here: Say to your AI: "Make a copy of my FilmCraft project film/in.fcproj as film/new.fcproj with my rendered correction s1 inserted as a frame hold, using the shots in film/shots and the renders in film/out." It runs the tool and tells you where the hold landed.
no_lists_because: It reads a FilmCraft project file, shot files and rendered media files and writes a new project file; it names no list of yours.
instructions: 1. Put each shot's file in a folder (film/shots/s1.json holds {"plate": {"source": "<the plate's media path in the project>", "frame": 48}}) and its three renders in film/out/s1/: s1-overlay-prores4444.mov, s1-narrator.wav and s1-sfx-music.wav.

2. Read the tool with tools:list {tool: "tool:insert-frame-holds-into-a-filmcraft-project-copy"}, then from the root of the Workshop checkout run its command with the project, a NEW output file, --shots, --out and the shot ids in order.

3. Read the last line: {"result": {"output", "inserts": [{"shot", "frames", "seconds", "at_seconds", "hold_frame"}]}} or {"error": ...}, which says what to change (a missing shot file, a missing render, a plate not in the project or a frame no clip holds).
4. Open the new project in FilmCraft; the input project is never written.

worked_examples.title: One correction becomes a half-second frame hold at 2 seconds
worked_examples.ask: Insert my rendered correction s1 into a copy of my FilmCraft project.
worked_examples.given: From tools/edit-a-copy-of-a-premiere-project/test/test_filmcraft_insert.py: the AI runs `python3 -I tools/edit-a-copy-of-a-premiere-project/do-work/filmcraft_insert_frame_holds.py film/in.fcproj film/new.fcproj --shots film/shots --out film/out s1`. The project is one 24 fps sequence with one 10 s clip of /made-up/plate.mp4 and its adjustment layer; film/shots/s1.json is {"id": "s1", "plate": {"source": "/made-up/plate.mp4", "frame": 48}}; film/out/s1/ holds a 12-frame ProRes 4444 overlay and two 0.5 s wav files. I ran this exact command, so the answer is observed.
worked_examples.hands_back: The first line printed is "s1: inserted 12 frames (0.500 s) at 2.000 s, hold = source frame 48", and the last line is {"result": {"output": "film/new.fcproj", "inserts": [{"shot": "s1", "frames": 12, "seconds": 0.5, "at_seconds": 2.0, "hold_frame": 48}]}}. In film/new.fcproj the sequence is named "Main + corrections", the first video track holds the clip to frame 48, a 12-frame hold of frame 48, then the rest moved 12 frames later; the overlay is on video track 3 and the voice and music files on audio tracks 2 and 3.
